summary: Harjot Oberoi works in religious studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He earned degrees from St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University, and held a chair in Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia around 1987.
Harogadde Manappa Nayak was an Indologist and linguist who served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1961–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin was an anthropologist and linguist who earned his bachelor's from UC Berkeley and his PhD from Yale. He taught at Columbia in 1955, followed by long tenures at Yale University and the Peabody Museum of Natural History (1974–1996).

Harold G. Coward is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from McMaster University (~1969–1973). He was a professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992) and later director at the University of Victoria (~1992–2002).

Harold Hargreaves was a British archaeologist and Indologist. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India in various capacities, including Frontier Circle Superintendent (~1914–1931) and Deputy Director General (1928–1931), having previously been headmaster at Government High School, Amritsar.

Harold Scheub earned his master's at the University of Michigan and his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–1969). After teaching posts at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he was a long-time professor at UW-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Harold Walter Bailey specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under F. W. Thomas. He taught at SOAS (1929) and held the Sanskrit chair at Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was a historian and Indologist who studied at Aligarh Muslim University and the University of Oxford, and completed postdoctoral work under Ghulam Yazdani. He held posts at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College, and Zakir Husain Delhi College.

Harry Falk is an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gaya Charan Tripathi. He served on the faculty at the University of Freiburg (~1979–1993) and as professor and Director at the Free University of Berlin (1993–2012).

Hartmut Buescher is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhal Tripathi. He has held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library (attested 2007).
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme and held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel was an Indologist who worked in the Oriental Department of the Royal Library of Berlin (attested 1982–1994) and directed projects for the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989–2008).

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Nagasaki University from approximately 1982 to 2003.
Haruka Yanagisawa was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who held academic posts at Chiba University (~1984–1996) and the University of Tokyo (~1996–2005).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her MA (1994) and PhD (2001) at the University of California, Los Angeles, under the supervision of Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Groningen and Leiden under Hans T. Bakker and Tilmann Vetter, and has held posts at Oxford, the University of Pennsylvania (2002–2006), and the University of Hamburg (from 2006).

Harushige Kōzu was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He held teaching posts at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and served as professor and dean at Musashi University (1968).

Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2001).

Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1934–1936) and served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1945–1946).
